_comment: Phase 5 juice tunables: particles, screen shake and hitstop. Every number the effects use lives here; src/fx/ only holds the mechanism. Deleting this file (or the art it names) disables the effects and leaves the game fully playable.

_fields.frames: columns in that row, played at 'fps' over the particle's life
_fields.angle_deg: [min, max] launch angle; 0 is +x, negative is up
_fields.aim: rotate angle_deg to face the direction passed to the burst
_fields.spread_px: radius the burst is scattered over
_fields.fade: fade alpha out over the particle's life

shake._comment: Amplitude is capped again in camera_controller.gd: shake is an offset inside the tile cull margin, never a change of screen.

hitstop._comment: Hard ceiling as well as per-preset values: a freeze that outlived its welcome would read as a soft-lock.

darkness._comment: World 4, Termite Deeps. A level turns this on with "darkness": 0.86 in data/ambience.json (or an object overriding any field below). It is a full-screen shade quad plus one additive pool that follows the player — the same two mechanisms AmbienceLayer already draws for the vignette and the authored lights, so a dark level costs two more quads and nothing else. Defaults live here rather than in ambience.gd because src/fx/ holds the mechanism and data/ holds every number.
darkness._why_visual_only: The Route Prover cannot see light. A level whose solvability depended on what you could see would be unprovable, so darkness never reaches collision, movement or the tile flags — it is drawn over the world and under the entities, and the player, enemies and pickups stay at full contrast.
